headline: Rushworth Keeps Goal And His Manager Guessing
deck: Semenyo's two goals and an assist top the team of the week; Rushworth benched by test211 despite a clean sheet, an assist and two saves.
body:
Semenyo is the man of the week and there is no argument in it. Two goals and an assist across the ninety, a forward doing the forward's job and then some, and test1 carried on his back. When a striker returns the full set nobody else in the eleven touches him.

The back is thin by design in a 1-2-5-3, so both defenders had to earn it and both did. Hall got on the scoresheet for test2, a goal from the back that no manager complains about, while Tarkowski added the assist and the clean sheet for testf and asked no questions. Behind them Rushworth is the story of the side. An assist, a clean sheet and two saves in goal, and his own manager at test211 left him on the bench. You do not often see a keeper post that line and watch it count for nothing at home.

The middle is where the side is built, five across it and every man returning. Groß was the pick, a goal and an assist and a clean sheet for 123, the complete midfield week. Barnes matched the creativity with two assists for testf and Willock found the net, so testf carry three of this eleven and would carry more on another week. Wirtz kept the assist and the sheet for test1, and Gomez did the same for test31, another man his manager sat down and another who made him regret it.

Up front Schade is the outlier, two assists and a clean sheet from a forward berth, a creator playing the point for 123. Kostoulas gave test31121 a goal and an assist and kept it tidy at the other end too. It is a front three that fetched and carried as much as it finished.

Unlucky to miss is a hard case to make against a side this full, but a fourth testf man would not have shamed anybody. The shape is the real tell: two at the back, five in the middle, and the week decided by midfielders who would not stop scoring.

And finally, a word about the men left on their own benches. Rushworth and Gomez both returned clean sheets and assists from the seats their managers chose, and they join a lengthening list this league keeps compiling. Davis, Gvardiol and Yalcouyé last time, these two now. At some point the benching stops being bad luck and starts being a habit worth naming.
